name: io.github.modaal-agent/screens-guide
title: screens.guide
description: Measured screen sizes, safe areas, corner radii and system bars of iOS and Android devices.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: Lists every device screens.guide measured: iPhones, iPads and Android phones, tablets and foldables. Each row gives the id the other tools take, the unit (pt or dp), each screen with its portrait window size, the runtime builds read, and the current one. Filter by platform or kind.

tools.name: get_device
tools.description: Returns a device's measured readings: window, pixels, safe-area insets, corner radii, size classes, the status bar, the app's top bar (navigationBar: UINavigationBar, or Material 3's TopAppBar), the bottom tab bar (tabBar: UITabBar, or Material 3's NavigationBar), content margin, reserved regions and fold, one reading per screen and rotation. Gives the current runtime's readings unless a runtime is named; narrow them by screen, orientation or rotation, which must agree when both are given (rotation 90 on a phone is landscape). A null value has its reason in the reading's `missing`, keyed by the field's dotted path, such as cornerRadii.measured.

device.description: A device id from list_devices, such as iphone-17 or pixel-8.

screen.description: A foldable's pose: closed, open, half-open or tent; every other device has main only.

rotation.description: The device's rotation; 90 puts its top edge on the window's left.

runtime.description: A runtime build such as 24A434, or a version such as 27.2 or 16, written exactly as list_devices gives it (27.0, not 27). A version names the device's current build when it is the current version, else that version's newest release build. The device's current build when omitted.

tools.name: compare_devices
tools.description: Compares 2 to 8 different devices side by side, one row per device and screen: window size, pixels, pixels per unit, safe-area insets, the safe area's rectangle and corner radii. Uses each device's current runtime and its reading at rotation 0 unless an orientation or runtime is named. At rotation 0 a foldable's open screen can be landscape, as the Pixel Fold's open and half-open screens are; name an orientation to compare like with like.

items.description: A device id from list_devices, such as iphone-17 or pixel-8.

runtime.description: A runtime build such as 24A434, or a version such as 27.2 or 16, written exactly as list_devices gives it (27.0, not 27). A version names the device's current build when it is the current version, else that version's newest release build. The device's current build when omitted.

tools.name: check_layout
tools.description: Checks up to 200 frames of a screen's layout against a device's measured window: whether each frame reaches outside the window, into a safe-area inset, past the display's rounded corner, under the status bar or the app's top or bottom bar, across a foldable's fold, or into a reserved region such as a camera. Each finding gives its numbers; a frame near a rounded corner gets the concentric radius. Frames are in the device's unit, in window coordinates from the top left. Without screen, a foldable is checked on its first screen, closed (the cover display). Orientation and rotation must agree when both are given. The request body is at most 64 KiB, so keep frame names short.

device.description: A device id from list_devices, such as iphone-17 or pixel-8.

screen.description: A foldable's pose: closed, open, half-open or tent; every other device has main only. A foldable's first screen, closed, when omitted.

runtime.description: A runtime build such as 24A434, or a version such as 27.2 or 16, written exactly as list_devices gives it (27.0, not 27). A version names the device's current build when it is the current version, else that version's newest release build. The device's current build when omitted.

orientation.description: The window shape; the reading at rotation 0 when neither this nor rotation is given.

rotation.description: The device's rotation; 90 puts its top edge on the window's left.

tools.name: convert_units
tools.description: Converts lengths on one device between its layout unit (pt on iOS, dp on Android) and physical pixels (px), at the device's measured scale or density. For dp to px on Android it also gives the whole pixel Compose's Dp.roundToPx() returns. Each value is between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000.

device.description: A device id from list_devices, such as iphone-17 or pixel-8.
